headline: ANTOFAGASTA H1: $4.5B Revenue, 72% Profit Surge — BUT Chile Catastrophe Cuts Copper Guidance as Los Pelambres Shuts on State-of-Catastrophe Declaration
snippet: Antofagasta PLC reported August 13 its strongest first-half margins on record — EBITDA of $2.8 billion at 63.4% on revenue of $4.5 billion, profit before tax up 72% to $2.0 billion, and net cash costs 8% lower at $1.22/lb — yet simultaneously slashed its 2026 full-year copper output guidance to 625,000–655,000 tonnes (from 650,000–700,000) after the Coquimbo Region government declared a 'state of catastrophe' following extraordinary snowfall that forced an orderly shutdown at Los Pelambres. The counterintuitive combination of record financial performance and a forced production cut in the same announcement captures the copper paradox of mid-2026: prices are high enough to reward what's being produced, but declining grades, aging infrastructure, and weather disruption are systematically narrowing the volume that reaches the market — making each new copper ounce in development more valuable.

headline: AYA GOLD & SILVER Q2 BLOWS OUT: $97M Revenue +151%, $48M Cash Flow +522% YoY — Morocco's Zgounder at Record 141 g/t Silver, 1.68 Moz AgEq
source_name: GlobeNewswire / Aya Gold & Silver Inc. (TSX: AYA)
snippet: Aya Gold & Silver Inc. (TSX: AYA) delivered August 14 a record-breaking Q2 2026: revenue of $97 million (up 151% year-over-year), operating cash flow of $48 million (up 522%), and net income of $35 million (up 305%), driven by 1.68 million silver equivalent ounces from Zgounder running at a record 141 g/t average silver feed grade and 3,889 t/d — plus a growing contribution from the new Boumadine gold-silver mine — ending the quarter with $183 million in cash. For silver investors, Aya's Q2 print is the clearest single-company demonstration of what $64/oz silver does to primary silver mine economics at high grade: Zgounder is generating some of the widest margins in the global silver mining industry, and $183 million cash positions the company to fund Boumadine development without equity dilution.

headline: NEWMONT BACKS HEADWATER'S JUPITER: $30M Nevada Earn-In, Up to 75% Stake — Walker Lane Epithermal Requires 1.5 Moz AuEq PFS to Earn Full Interest
snippet: Headwater Gold Inc. announced August 13 that Newmont Corporation will earn up to a 75% interest in the Jupiter Project in Nevada's southern Walker Lane belt through staged US$30 million in exploration expenditures — with a firm $2.5 million minimum over 24 months, 51% at $10 million within 48 months, and an additional 24% by funding a PFS targeting minimum 1.5 million ounce gold-equivalent — marking Newmont's third earn-in with Headwater and by far its largest. For junior investors tracking major-company validation signals: a world-class gold producer volunteering US$30 million of its own exploration capital into a private junior's district-scale Nevada epithermal property is the clearest publicly-available signal that Newmont's geology team believes Jupiter has multi-million-ounce potential not yet defined by drilling.

headline: GOGOLD Q3 FY2026: $26.3M RECORD CASH FLOW, $284M WAR CHEST Exceeds Los Ricos South Capex — Parral Hits 12-Year Silver-Gold Output High
source_name: Newsfile Corp / GoGold Resources Inc. (TSX: GGD)
snippet: GoGold Resources Inc. (TSX: GGD) announced August 12 record Q3 FY2026 operating cash flow of $26.3 million on $27.8 million in revenue from 419,986 silver equivalent ounces at its Parral mine in Chihuahua, Mexico — its twelfth consecutive operating year at Parral — ending the quarter with $284 million cash, which materially exceeds the $227 million initial capital requirement for the already-permitted Los Ricos South project as per its feasibility study. GoGold is one of the handful of development-stage silver companies that can fund its next mine's construction entirely from existing cash and ongoing cash flow without issuing a single new share, making it the clearest non-dilutive silver development story for retail investors in the current market.

headline: AVINO Q2: NET INCOME +281%, $145M CASH, ZERO BANK DEBT — Silver at $68.90/oz Drives Strongest Operating Margin in Company History
source_name: Avino Silver & Gold Mines Ltd. (TSX/NYSE-A: ASM)
snippet: Avino Silver & Gold Mines Ltd. (TSX: ASM) reported August 12 that Q2 2026 net income after taxes surged 281% year-over-year to $10.9 million ($0.06/diluted share) on revenue of $26.8 million (up 23%), with 54% of revenues from silver at an average realized price of $68.90 per ounce — delivering EBITDA of $12.6 million (+69%) and a record cash position of $145 million with zero secured bank debt. Avino's balance sheet — $145 million cash, zero bank debt, and a producing Mexico silver mine — is the financial profile that insulates a small silver producer from the equity dilution cycle that destroys retail investor returns during corrections, while the operating leverage remains fully intact during silver rallies.

headline: NORTH SHORE URANIUM COMPLETES FIRST-EVER DRILL AT NEW MEXICO GRANTS DISTRICT — 13 Holes, 2,828m at Rio Puerco; Phase 2 Follows in Q4
source_name: Junior Mining Network / North Shore Uranium Ltd. (TSX-V: NSU)
snippet: North Shore Uranium Ltd. (TSX-V: NSU) announced August 13 the completion of its inaugural Phase 1 drill program at the Rio Puerco uranium project in New Mexico's Grants Uranium District — 13 rotary holes totaling 2,828 metres validating historical Kerr-McGee exploration data from the 1960s–70s — with detailed assay results pending and Phase 2 (up to 26 permitted holes, 5,975 total metres) planned for Q4 2026 after the monsoon season. The Grants Mineral Belt in northwest New Mexico hosts the most uranium-prospective geology in the continental US outside the Athabasca Basin, and the transition from 'permitted but undrilled' to 'actively drilling with confirmed historical targets' is the inflection where junior uranium stocks historically see sharpest institutional attention.

headline: CHILE 2026 COPPER FORECAST CUT TO 5.27M TONNES — 19-Year Production Low as Codelco + Antofagasta Shortfalls Compound Chile's Shrinking Share of Global Supply
snippet: Chile's government has revised its 2026 national copper production forecast down to 5.27 million tonnes — a figure that would represent the country's weakest output since 2007, and a further reduction of approximately 300,000 tonnes from the prior quarterly estimate — as weak H1 performance at Codelco (El Teniente down 26.5% in Q1 alone) compounds Antofagasta's July weather-driven guidance cut. Chile is now producing less copper than it did in 2010 while global demand has grown 35%, with its share of world production shrinking from 34% to approximately 21% — and each successive guidance cut strengthens the argument that the 200,000–400,000 tonne annual structural deficit projected through 2030 may prove understated, directly repricing the strategic value of copper development projects outside Chile.

headline: GOLD MINERS' HOTTEST FIVE-DAY RUN SINCE 2008: Single-Digit PE Multiples, Above-Average Dividends — September Fed Hike Odds Collapse to 44%
snippet: Gold mining stocks posted their best five-session run since 2008 through August 12 as sequentially tame CPI and PPI prints erased the Federal Reserve's near-term rate-hike case — driving September rate increase probability from 67% to 44% in a week — while gold held above $4,400 and silver approached $66 per ounce. For retail investors who have not yet repositioned into senior and mid-tier miners: the valuation disconnect remains extreme — quality gold producers are trading at single-digit forward earnings multiples while generating record free cash flow margins and paying above-average dividends, a combination that historically exists only at the early stages of an institutional re-rating cycle.

headline: GOLDSEEK: Gold's Orderly Retreat from 10-Week High Is Bullish — PPI Miss Validates $4,380 Floor, Confirms February Breakout Is Structural
snippet: In August 13 market commentary, GoldSeek argues that gold's retreat from the near-$4,500 two-month high to $4,349 on tame PPI data represents an orderly, technically healthy consolidation rather than a fundamental breakdown — with the interpretation that a softer-than-expected headline PPI (0.0% vs. 0.2% expected) combined with gold holding above $4,380 in subsequent sessions is actually more constructive than a vertical continuation, confirming the February–July falling wedge breakout is demand-driven rather than a short-squeeze artifact. The analysis gives junior gold mining investors the framework to distinguish between short-term volatility from macro data releases and the underlying structural bull trend — which for 12–36 month positions is the only signal that matters.

headline: GBM RESOURCES EXTENDS TWIN HILLS GOLD HOST 700M SOUTH — Queensland BXM Horizon Confirmed Beyond 309 Resource Boundary; 60% of Metres Still Awaiting Assay
source_name: Proactive Investors / GBM Resources Ltd. (ASX: GBM)
snippet: GBM Resources Ltd. (ASX: GBM) confirmed August 14 that step-out drilling at the Stella prospect within the Twin Hills Gold Project in Queensland has extended the prospective Milled Matrix Breccia horizon at least 700 metres south of the existing 309 mineral resource boundary — gold mineralization returned in every hole including a best of 8 metres at 1.31 g/t gold from 126 metres — with approximately 60% of drilled metres still awaiting assay. The 700-metre host horizon extension beyond the current resource envelope is significant for its geometry, not the individual intercept grades: a 700-metre step-out of the BXM sequence in a structurally-controlled Queensland gold system typically precedes a material resource boundary expansion once all assays are incorporated, and GBM has completed approximately 25,000 metres of Stage 2 resource-development drilling since February 2026.
